system: Essentially coincidental. Mundane scanners take 3 or more successes, special or Technocratic ones 5 or more. A failure rejects the card; a botch likely ruins the card and glitches the system, which sets off alarms.

name: Glitch a Security Scanner
summary: Throw faults into a body scanner, X-ray, breathalyzer or retina reader so it reports what you want and you walk through. Not enough for scans guarding high-security areas.
system: Needs 3 or more successes for the result you want. Too few successes or a failure gets you a closer look from the guards; a botch sets off every alarm in the building.

combos.note: Data only: a clean false reading

name: The All-Access Pass
summary: Combine a prepared fake credential, a mental push and a commanding presence (plus props and Backgrounds like Fame or Rank) to stride past security as someone far too important to check.
system: Against ordinary security and no real resistance, the combination may get you through without rolling at all.

name: Flip Traffic Lights
summary: Turn a traffic signal in your favor with a quick jolt. The other drivers may not react well to the sudden change, so accidents can follow.
system: Coincidental unless you are absurdly obvious about it, since plenty of people yell at traffic lights.

optional.purpose: pick the best moment for the switch

name: Part the Crowd
summary: Reshape the flow of a crowd or traffic so a path opens for you, pursuers get stuck behind, or both. A jam that has nowhere to go cannot be redirected this way.
system: Most crowds take 2-5 successes, dense ones a few more; riots and stampedes are easier to scatter than orderly crowds. A Mind add-on costs 3 or more extra successes. The Entropy version is usually coincidental; physically shoving people or cars around with Forces turns vulgar if they go flying.

combos.note: physically push traffic; Forces 3 for more

optional.purpose: reach a huge crowd or freeway beyond your sight
make people scramble out of your way or cover your escape

name: Levitate and Float Along
summary: Shift gravity and inertia to lift a person or object off the ground and drift it around. Living beings are harder to levitate than objects.
system: Forces 2 lifts about one person (up to 300 pounds), Forces 3 about two tons, Forces 4 a small building, Forces 5 nearly anything short of a mountain. Rough flight may call for Dexterity or Wits + Athletics.

combos.note: an object you keep aloft yourself

optional.purpose: lock the levitation on with mental power
lock the levitation on with vital energy

name: Fly a Broom, Carpet or Car
summary: Make an object that was never meant to fly, from a broom to a sports car, carry you through the air. Binding the Effect to the object keeps it up without your constant attention.
system: A simple rule: 20 MPH per success spent on flight, so 100 MPH takes 5 successes (divide successes as usual). Heavy objects need more Forces: Forces 3 handles a car. No seat belts, so hold on.

combos.note: a light object like a broom or carpet

name: Fly Like an Eagle
summary: Grow working wings, or strap on homemade mechanical ones, and fly.
system: Muscle-powered wings move up to 20 yards per action for 3 actions per Stamina dot before fatigue. After that, a Willpower roll (difficulty 6) buys another 3 actions per dot at half speed; more rolls keep going at 1 bashing level per action, then lethal once bashing runs out.

optional.purpose: power mechanical wings with a Quintessence battery

name: Teleport to a Location
summary: Step from where you are to another place without crossing the space between. Seen or familiar places are far easier to hit than unknown ones.
system: Successes by destination: 1 within your perception; 2 a very familiar place like home or Sanctum; 3 familiar, recently seen or known through intimate data; 4 visited briefly, an IP address or seen online; 5 only heard described or given coordinates; 6+ totally blind. A failure fizzles; a botch is an immediate physical Paradox backlash as you arrive inside something (bashing for a bump, lethal for a crash, aggravated for landing inside an object or person, who may be hurt too), plus +3 to your spotting difficulties for a while. Calling the jump a lucky taxi does not make it coincidental.
coincidentalIf: you vanish into darkness or smoke and a witness could believe you simply went somewhere else; vanishing in front of people is vulgar with witnesses, and vanishing unseen is still vulgar without witnesses

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Time and Distance

name: Hail a Coincidental Cab
summary: Instead of teleporting and pretending it was a taxi, use magick to get a real cab to you: call one with your thoughts, or arrange to be at the curb just as one rolls up.

combos.note: catch one at just the right moment

name: Spot the New Location
summary: Take a turn to look ahead at where you mean to teleport, so you do not jump in blind.
system: Roll Intelligence + Awareness, difficulty 6 (higher in darkness, storms or stress; lower in bright light or calm focus). On a success the destination counts as within your perception on the teleport chart, so the jump itself needs only 1 success.

name: The Blink
summary: Hop through several locations in quick succession rather than making a single jump, for surprise and mobility in a fight.
system: Add up the teleport-chart successes for each stop, then add 1 per blink: three blinks within sight cost 3 + 3 = 6. Each blink is an action; to blink and act in one turn, roll the lower of Arete or the action's dice pool. If cast ahead of time you can fast-cast between blinks. Vulgar.

name: The Batman: Vanish in Shadow
summary: Wrap yourself in shadow or smoke and muffled sound, and when it clears you are gone. A variant lets you pop in and out of cover, strike, and turn up somewhere else.
system: Forces hides you while Correspondence moves you. It can stay coincidental as long as nobody could see you disappear impossibly or cross space in a way normal physics cannot explain.

optional.purpose: leave onlookers with an uneasy chill

coincidentalIf: no one can witness you vanishing or moving in a way physics cannot explain

name: Forge a Tether
summary: Bind an object or being to yourself so you can pull it to you through space from wherever it is.
system: A tethered thing always counts as within your perception on the teleport chart. You need at least as many Correspondence dots as the highest other Sphere used. Lasts the normal Duration unless made permanent.

combos.note: a complex living being, such as a cat or person

name: Everywhere at Once: Multiple Selves
summary: Send copies of yourself to several places at once. Plain Correspondence makes them mirror images; with more magick each self acts on its own in its own place.
system: Base successes come from the least familiar destination, plus 1 per self; Mind adds 1, Life adds 1 per self. Example: 3 selves, one to a described place, independent: 5 + 3 + 1 + 3 = 12. Each self takes damage on its own; on reuniting all damage lands on you. A self that dies deals you 1 aggravated level that heals only once all selves are back; if all copies die, so do you, and killing the original ends them all. The Avatar stays in the original. Vulgar.

optional.purpose: keep the selves' senses from getting scrambled
let each self act independently

name: The Warp-Gate
summary: Tear a brief hole in space to pass through, open just long enough to get in, usually to shortcut a journey. Spot the destination first.
system: Stays open a turn or two. Roll only the teleport-chart successes: 2 to get home, 5 for a place you saw online. Gates are vulgar except where local reality, such as a fitting Sanctum, allows them.

combos.note: a larger gate, for others or a vehicle

name: The Location Portal
summary: Build a lasting doorway between two places, from a rune-carved arch to an ordinary door that opens somewhere else. Wise mages set both ends up in Sanctums or Chantries first and add wards.
system: 10 successes make it permanent, plus the teleport-chart successes (2 more for a very familiar place, 5 for one only heard of). Bigger portals and more safeguards cost more. Vulgar unless local reality allows it; if either end is a place where it would be vulgar, the whole thing is.

optional.purpose: open the far end into an Umbral Realm
open onto a personal Astral Realm, dreamworld or Demesne

name: Bridge Similar Locations
summary: Fold space so that two similar places join: a hotel door opens into a club on another continent, a forest path ends in a different forest.
system: Base 5 successes plus the teleport-chart value of the far end: 7 for a very familiar place, 10 for one only heard about. A quick blur onlookers can shrug off may pass as coincidental; open spatial weirdness is vulgar. Big space-warping feats like this start at difficulty 6 or more and cause at least 5 Paradox.

name: Stretch or Shrink Distance
summary: Warp space for as long as it lasts: a short hallway runs for miles, or a long road shrinks to a stroll.
system: Successes follow the Magickal Feats chart at the Storyteller's call: shrinking downtown Seattle to Mount Rainier might take 6, Seattle to Berlin 10 or more. Subtle warps may pass as coincidental; visible Escher-style ones are vulgar and draw powerful attention. Permanent warps take at least 10 successes, gross ones 20 or more.

name: Escher Architecture: Bend Local Physics
summary: Remake a small area into an impossible landscape: stairs that loop, rooms that fold, fire sculptures and upward-flowing water, even trees of flesh and talking hills. People inside can use it as if it were normal.
system: Successes by the Magickal Feats chart, and it needs many. Making it permanent costs 10 extra successes and Quintessence: 1-2 points for small touches, 5 or more for big works. Life 5 is still needed for living things to swim in fire or breathe sunlight. Vulgar, but more or less normal inside a Sanctum or Realm that fits your reality.

combos.note: elements and energies that behave impossibly
living, flesh-warped scenery and adapted lifeforms

name: Transpose Locations
summary: Stack two or more places on top of each other like layers, so a car in one city can turn onto a road in another. Weather bleeds between layers, satellites go haywire, and anyone who wanders across stays where they end up.
system: 10 base successes plus 10 per layer for pieces up to a quarter-mile square; 10 more per piece for each extra quarter-mile square. Each 10 minutes of Duration costs 1 more success (21 for 10 minutes, 23 for 30). No modifiers: difficulty 9 without witnesses, 10 with. At least 5 Paradox per 10 minutes even on a success. Can never be made permanent. Always vulgar.

name: Moving Mountains
summary: Rip a whole place, from a shed to a mountain, out of its spot and set it down somewhere else, leaving a hole or a blank surface behind.
system: Base successes by size: 3 tiny (car, tent), 5 small (van, hut), 7 noticeable (small house), 10 medium (suburban home), 13 sizable (mansion, park), 15 large (estate, small hill), 17 huge (office block, city block), 20+ vast (skyscraper, mountain). Lasts the normal Duration, then the place crumbles; making it permanent takes 10 more successes and at least 10 Quintessence. At least 5 Paradox even on a success. The moved place takes on its new climate. Vulgar.

optional.purpose: keep the living things that come along alive
keep those living things from panicking
keep the Umbrascape at both ends from being scrambled

name: Wrack a Ghost
summary: Force a ghost to show up, pin it in place, and make it hurt until it talks or obeys, or simply destroy it. Cruel, and guaranteed to make the dead hostile.
system: Remains, fetters or things tied to the death count as personal items on the difficulty chart, and threatening a fetter is another lever over the ghost.

combos.note: compel it to appear and trap it there

name: Bind a Ghost into an Object
summary: Seal a ghost inside a thing, as a threat, a punishment, or a way to get rid of a dangerous spectre.

name: Thicken the Gauntlet Against Ghosts
summary: Harden the barrier to the dead inside a circle of salt, a pentacle or a shield grid, so ghosts have a harder time reaching through.
system: Each success raises the local Gauntlet by 1 for the Duration.

name: Ward Against Ghostly Powers
summary: Shield an area and the people in it from the death-powers of ghosts, without changing the spirit world around it.
system: The first 2 successes set the ward; each further success takes 1 success off any ghostly attack on the protected. Spend 1 more success per extra person warded. A wraith trying to break the ward gets 1 extra die per Fetter dot when the ward stands between it and its fetter, but loses those dice if the fetter is built into the ward.

name: Wall Off or Banish Ghosts
summary: Raise walls of ephemera against the dead, drive spirits away, or exorcise a ghost from a place or person. Handy against vicious spectres.
system: Stronger workings may need Spirit 5. See Exorcism in the Uncanny Influence rules.

name: The Song of Flies: Read a Death
summary: Study a murder scene, grave, body or murder weapon for how someone died, who was there and what happened. Works best where the death left a strong mark, and can leave the mage scarred by what they see.

combos.note: read the Resonance the death left
look back in time at the death

name: Self-Possession by a Ghost
summary: Open yourself as a willing horse for a ghost, keeping some control while borrowing whatever Abilities it chooses to share. The ghost gets a living body to ride for a while.
system: You and the ghost make an extended, resisted Willpower roll, each against the other's Willpower; the first to 10 successes controls the body. Afterward you need a day to two weeks of rest and pick up a dot or two of the ghost's Resonance, and you count as a personal item for dealing with that ghost from then on. No Arcanoi or Charms pass over. Obvious possession is usually vulgar, though some places like New Orleans accept it from the right people.

name: Possess Another with a Ghost
summary: Bind a ghost into another living creature's flesh to sway its moods, drive its body, fight it for control, or rip it apart from inside.
system: The tear-apart version deals aggravated damage. Always vulgar, and especially foul unless ghost and host both agree.

combos.note: drop the ghost in and let them fight for control
the ghost tears the victim apart

name: Animate Dead Remains
summary: Make dead flesh or bones move again, from a twitching finger to a walking corpse. This gives no mind or life, only motion, unless you invite or lock a ghost in.
system: Successes: 1 for a small piece (finger, heart), 2 a hand or foot, 3 a head or arm, 4 limbs plus torso, 5 a whole body. Remains keep rotting; slowing it only delays the end. Scavengers love animated remains.

optional.purpose: invite a ghost into the remains
lock a ghost into the remains
slow the rot
slow the rot

name: Raise a Zombie
summary: Create a walking dead thing by one of four grim methods, from swapping a living soul for a ghost to locking a murdered person's mind inside their own corpse.
system: Unless made permanent, the zombie collapses when the Duration ends. It rots like any animated remains. All methods are extremely vulgar.

combos.note: replace a living person's mind and soul with a ghost
a corpse made into a Fetish ridden by a ghost
kill the person and trap their mind in the corpse
destroy a living soul and move a ghost in

name: Build a Frankencritter
summary: The technomancer's take on raising the dead: surgery, formulae and current turn dead parts into something that moves, thinks, or refuses to finish dying.
system: Uses the same rules as zombies. The galvanized kind runs on twitchy reflexes and does not last long; the kind with a mind has its own will and may ignore you. Extremely vulgar.

combos.note: give a reanimated corpse a working mind
freeze time in a dying body and keep it running

name: Revive the Newly Dead
summary: Bring back someone who died in the last five minutes or so: repair what killed them, hold the soul in place and jump-start the body. Much easier than true resurrection.
coincidentalIf: the death was minutes ago and a revival is believable, like CPR on a drowning or heart attack victim; bringing back someone beheaded or burned to a crisp is vulgar

name: Resurrect the Dead
summary: Truly raise the dead: turn the corpse back into a living body, restore the mind and fetch back the departed soul. A soul long gone may be hard to find, and what comes back may not be the same person.
system: Older corpses need Matter as well, more the further decay has gone. Finding a long-dead soul may mean a journey into the Underworld or afterlife Realms. Totally vulgar unless the subject died only minutes ago.

combos.note: a corpse dead for some time

optional.purpose: restore body and mind to a save point just before death (very hard)

name: Necrosynthesis
summary: Pump death-energy through a living body so it rots with leprous corruption, or even hatches maggots that eat the victim from inside.
system: Deals aggravated damage. Casting it automatically gives you a dot of Jhor or Entropic Synergy, and Morbidity Quiet likely follows at your next Paradox. Extremely vulgar.

optional.purpose: breed maggots inside the victim
combine with Gilgul to destroy the Avatar too

name: Summon a Creature from Elsewhere on Earth
summary: Pull a living creature from some other place in the physical world to your summoning spot. A tiny one, house-cat size or smaller, needs far less power.
system: Takes 2 to 10 successes, more for big creatures and long distances. Nearly always vulgar; the Storyteller may allow exceptions.

optional.purpose: win the creature over to your side right away
sway the creature to your side right away

name: Summon a Spirit Through the Gauntlet
summary: Call out to a spirit, then drag it across the Gauntlet into the material world; with more rank you can bring a whole group over. What arrives still has to be bargained with.
system: A nature spirit in its own element is easy: open the Gauntlet and let it through. A major entity has to be fetched from its home Realm for 10 to 15 successes or more. Bargaining: if you score no successes on a roll, the spirit may roll Willpower (difficulty your Spirit rank +5) to leave or attack; the Pact is a resisted Willpower contest where each side needs successes equal to the other's Willpower. Quintessence offered to a spirit becomes Essence point for point.

name: Summon a Demon, Angel or Other Great Entity
summary: Open a gateway for a mighty being such as an angel or a demon, a big Bygone or a vast alien, and tie it to the material world through an enchanted item, its True Name, or both.
system: Pulling it from its home Realm takes 10 to 15 successes; truly powerful beings from far planes take at least 15, plus 10 more while the Avatar Storm lasts. Needs a prepared space and full protocols, and is vulgar.

name: House an Elemental in Its Element

name: Build a Golem
summary: Shape material into a body, bind a spirit into it and quicken it with Quintessence: a golem.
system: Spirit binds the entity, Matter forms the body, Prime animates it. Every 2 successes give the golem 1 Durability and 1 Structure (M20 pp. 439-440); if attacks bring those to zero it breaks apart and the spirit goes free.

name: Ward Against Elemental Energies
summary: Bar a kind of energy, such as fire, electricity, light or sound, at a threshold or a surface. The same ward can make a doorway airtight, which matters next to a vacuum.
system: Intense radiation and nuclear forces need Forces 5, and so Correspondence 5, since Correspondence must be at least your highest other Sphere in the ward; shutting out a nuclear blast takes Matter 5 too. Price: 1 Quintessence for the ward plus 1 per objective, and each objective adds 1 to the successes needed. Successes set how long it holds: 1 a turn, 2 a scene, 3 a day, 4 a story, 5 six months; permanent takes 10 plus 1 per objective and 1 more Quintessence per Sphere. As a major ward it costs 1 extra Quintessence per Sphere (2 per Sphere if permanent). Paradox: 1 point per dot of the highest Sphere, +1 if someone watched, added to your wheel without a backlash unless you botch.

optional.purpose: make the seal watertight as well

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

name: Lock a Ward into an Object, Element or Creature
summary: Build a ward into the Pattern of the thing that carries it: floorboards, a door, a gadget, a fire, or a living being. With Prime it becomes a traveling ward that goes where the thing goes, and nothing it bars can touch that thing.
system: Air, light, heat and radiation are too thin to hold a ward, though shadows oddly can. A traveling ward costs 1 more Quintessence and pushes barred things off its surface instead of stopping them at a line; it only covers what it sits on, so a warded jacket leaves your legs open. Every 3 extra successes push the barrier one more yard out (the cost chart lists 3 Quintessence per yard). Pressing your own warded thing into what it bars cancels the ward for you, but not when someone else does it. Correspondence must match the highest other Sphere, so Forces 5 needs Correspondence 5.

summary: Keep particular people out by their mental fingerprint: the ward recognizes them and turns their mind away from going in.
system: Each barred person is a separate objective costing 1 Quintessence. You must have read the person's mind before setting the ward. Spirit 4 (or Dimensional Science) is needed against werecreatures, Umbral entities and other deeply spiritual beings. name: Major Ward: The Ban
summary: The simplest major ward: a kind of creature or spirit, or one named individual, cannot touch you or aim its powers and weapons straight at you.
system: At least 5 successes on a vulgar roll. One named spirit needs its True Name or another link (a Fetter, a sigil, a tied object); one particular mortal needs an item from their life plus Mind 4. It does not stop indirect attacks through other people or things, and it drops if you botch a Contest of Wills. As a major ward it costs 1 extra Quintessence per Sphere (2 per Sphere if permanent). Paradox: 1 point per dot of the highest Sphere, +1 if someone watched, added to your wheel without a backlash unless you botch.

name: Major Ward: The Luck Ward
summary: Keep misfortune out of an area, or invite it in, and blunt hostile Entropy magick. Casinos use it against cheating mages; gamblers carry it as a charm.
system: When a non-combat event inside could turn out lucky or unlucky, you roll Arete automatically, with no action needed. The Storyteller decides which events count. One use per Quintessence spent on the ward; more uses cost 1 Quintessence each. Entropy 2 is the minimum; more works too.

Lasts the normal Duration unless held with Time 4 or made permanent.

optional.purpose: keep the ward going past the normal Duration

coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Psychic Ward
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Psychic Ward

name: Major Ward: The Paradigm Ward
summary: Seal a place against followers of chosen paradigms or practices: magick they work through those beliefs counts as vulgar with witnesses on your side of the gate.
system: Each barred paradigm or practice costs 3 more successes and 3 more Quintessence on top of the ward itself (three of them: +9 and +9); they are the objectives, so no separate objective cost. You can bar one form of a practice and allow another at the same price. Optional: mages with lower Arete than yours may lose their Spheres there. Optional pain on entry, 5 Quintessence each: a Psychic Blast, an Entropy assault on their beliefs, or both for 10; one attack per Quintessence invested.
coincidentalIf: Set up inside a Sanctum or Realm that is built around your own magick.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Paradigm Ward
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: The Paradigm Ward

name: Unweave a Ward
summary: Tear down someone else's ward with countermagick. You need at least a dot in every Sphere the ward was built with.
system: Arete roll at difficulty 7 (8 under the Reckoning), spending as much Quintessence as went into the ward. Each success cancels one of the ward's successes and you need one more than it had, so 16 against a 15-success ward. An unwoven ward is gone for good. For a ward of unknown origin the Storyteller picks its Spheres and successes.

combos.note: plus 1 dot in each other Sphere used in the ward

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Penetrating a Ward

name: Wrack a Spirit: Spiritual Damage
summary: Hurt a bound or warded spirit to back up your threats. At the lower rank you simply wound it; at mastery you can twist and tear its very form apart.
system: Normal damage, which the spirit heals at its normal rate. Any wracking makes a lasting enemy of the spirit, so it is a last resort.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Ephemeral Mutation
summary: Reshape a spirit's form the way Life 4 or 5 reshapes a person: painful and humiliating, and dangerous if you make it look like prey for other spirits.
system: Deals the attack's damage on top. Most spirits can reform without much trouble.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Psychic Agony
summary: Attack a spirit's sense of self, as with Psychic Shatter: agony without injury to its form. Pushed hard enough, it can drive the spirit mad.
system: Works on spirits despite the usual limits on mental attacks against them, because the rites are made for it.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Primal Disruption
summary: Scramble the Quintessence a spirit is made of. At the lower ranks it is like Rubbing the Bones; at mastery you blast its form apart across the landscape.
system: A disintegrated spirit can heal, but it takes far longer than usual, by Storyteller call.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Prolonged Agony
summary: Add Time to any spirit wrack: extra actions for more attacks, or a time bubble that keeps the pain going until you stop it or a trigger fires.
system: Spirit 3 is the cheapest wrack to build on; use the Spheres of whichever wrack you choose. This earns enmity that lasts for ages.

combos.note: lock the spirit in a bubble of time

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit
Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Entropic Dispersal
summary: Turn decay on the idea behind a spirit and scatter its conceptual self, for a while or maybe for good.
system: Deals normal damage too. Spirits usually reform in a few months; one with 10 Essence or less never does, while famous beings reform in minutes. Minor spirits scatter at 0 Essence; great ones may need two or three times their Essence in damage. Icons of the human imagination cannot really be dispersed.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Wrack a Spirit: Spiritual Imprisonment
summary: Build a small spirit Realm as a jail, bind the spirit to it and send it away. It stays there until it breaks the Gauntlet Cage, the Realm collapses, or you free it.
system: Can be combined with the other tortures and with Prolonged Agony, which marks the mage as a brute and stains their Resonance.

source.section: Summoning, Binding, Bargaining, and Warding: Wracking the Spirit

name: Spot Temporal Disturbances
summary: Keep an exact sense of the current time and notice the ripples left behind by Time magick: rewinds, loops, triggers, anchor points and travellers popping out of the timestream.
system: Noticing a disturbance is usually a Perception + Awareness roll; bigger Effects leave bigger ripples. They can show up as waves in the air, ghostly sounds from other times, ticking clocks, slow-motion patches or deja vu.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: The Basics
Time Distortion and Travel: Temporal Disturbances

name: Speed Yourself Up or Slow Others Down
summary: Stretch time around yourself to get extra actions in a turn, or squeeze it around someone else to take actions away from them.
system: Two successes per extra action gained, or per action taken away from another character. Speeding yourself up does not count toward the Repeated Time Effects penalty.
coincidentalIf: you take only one or two extra actions a turn, which can pass as a burst of speed; three or more a turn is vulgar

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: The Basics
Common Magickal Effects: Time and Distance

name: The Perfect Moment
summary: Sense exactly when to act so a mundane task goes better: the right moment to walk in, crack a joke, throw a punch or juggle. Harder, more involved tasks call on extra Spheres to read the situation.
system: Cast the Effect with your focus first. Each Arete success then lowers the difficulty of one Attribute + Ability roll by 1, to at most -3. It cannot lower an Arete roll, except when used to prepare a ritual in advance, and even then by no more than -3. Needs time to set up, so it is little use in a fast fight.

optional.purpose: spot the right place as well as the right time
get yourself to the right place at the right time
read the odds
nudge the odds toward the perfect moment
time your move to the flow of energies
bend those energies to fit your timing
sense who is around and how healthy and receptive they are
read the moods of the people involved
read their thoughts to know when they are most open
spot flaws in an object
feel the currents of Quintessence
steer those currents toward the moment
read the spirit of the times

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: The Perfect Moment

name: Total Recall
summary: Relive a past event from someone's own memory in full sensory detail, as if it were happening now. The memory stays as subjective as the original experience, though the viewer may catch details missed at the time.
system: More successes give a clearer and more accurate memory. Nothing the person could not perceive back then can be recovered. Whether it can recall things that have not happened yet is up to the Storyteller.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Total Recall

name: Thicken the Walls of Time
summary: Make the local flow of time heavy and stubborn so that other mages have a harder time working Time magick near you.
system: Each success you score takes one success off another mage's Time Effects. Past five successes, time around you starts to stutter: clocks skip, speech and movement drag, and everyone feels heavy. That is easy to miss out in the wilds but obvious in busy places like cities or parties.
coincidentalIf: you use no more than five successes

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Thickening the Walls of Time

name: Time Loop
summary: Freeze an area and roll it back to an earlier moment while you alone keep moving, so you can act differently the second time around.
system: Counts as a Magickal Feat of Time: 3 successes for yourself, 4 for one other person, 5 for a few people or a 10-foot square, 8 for a 25-foot square, 10-20 for larger areas, 20+ for a huge area. Add 2 successes per turn rewound. Going back adds +3 difficulty and multiplies Paradox by the turns rewound. Each further Time Effect in the same scene must score more successes than the one before.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Rewinding Time
Time Distortion and Travel: Magickal Feats of Time
Common Magickal Effects: Time and Distance

name: Reboot Another Person
summary: Send someone else back a few turns with their memories intact, so they can replay events knowing what is coming. The rest of the world repeats itself until they change something.
system: Each rebooted person beyond yourself costs 3 or more extra successes on top of the 2 per turn rewound. Rewinding adds +3 difficulty and stacks Paradox per turn. The Storyteller may cap reboots at five turns. Cannot undo a vampire's curse. Rebooting only yourself takes Life 3, Mind 1 and Time 3.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Rewinding Time

name: Accelerated Aging or Youth
summary: Fast-forward the aging of a person, creature or object until it withers or crumbles, or run it backward to make it young or new again. It works on the whole subject at once, never on a single part.
system: Successes depend on how much aging, not how many years: 3 minor, 4 noticeable, 5 severe, 8 decrepit, 10-20 near destruction, 20+ aged out of existence. Reversing age adds +3 difficulty. Vampires, werecreatures, mummies and fae just take lethal damage equal to the successes and recover their years; spirits and ghosts are immune.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Accelerated Youth or Decay
Time Distortion and Travel: Aging the Night-Folk

name: Disrupt Heartbeat Rhythm
summary: Throw a person's heartbeat out of its natural rhythm. You can upset the timing of the heart, but you cannot run it in a different time-stream from the rest of the body.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Accelerated Youth or Decay

name: Temporal Anchor Point
summary: Fix a point in time you can return to after travelling or stepping out of time. The anchor can be a set alarm or clock, a mantra, an icon, a place or a memorable staged event, depending on your focus.
system: Without an anchor, any trip through time is one-way and the Storyteller decides where you end up. Returning also needs Time 4 and only works if the anchor still exists and you can reach it. Anyone with Time 1 can spot an anchor, so hide it well. Setting it in a Sanctum or other secluded place makes the return less likely to draw Paradox.

optional.purpose: return to the anchor from far away in space

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Freeze a Moment in Time
summary: Stop a single event in mid-motion, like a falling glass, a bullet or a car crash. When the freeze ends, everything carries on along its old path unless you changed it in the meantime.
system: Base successes by size of event: a falling teacup 1, a looming train wreck 5-10 or more. Add successes for longer durations by the dividing successes chart (one day +2, six months +5). Anyone else touching the frozen scene ends it at once; you can end it whenever you like.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Temporal Suspension
summary: Put one subject into stasis: stop a body's life processes, hold an object, energy or place unchanged, keep something from decaying, lock a spirit outside time, or even hold a feeling, memory or train of thought in place.
system: Lasts the normal Duration; extend it with the dividing successes rule. Small subjects are easy (a mouse, 1-2 successes); big or complex ones like a tank or a set of memories take 5 or more.

combos.note: stop decay; also add the Sphere of the place, object or body
a memory, idea or state of sanity

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Contingency Trigger Effect
summary: Hang another Effect in time so it only goes off when a chosen condition is met: a kiss, a cat crossing a doorstep, a band finally splitting up.
system: Base successes depend on the scale of the held Effect, per the Feats of Time Magick chart; it lasts until the condition happens. While waiting it sits in a temporal ripple that Time mages can notice and counter.

optional.purpose: tie the held Effect to an object
tie the held Effect to a living being

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Time Bubble Prison
summary: Wrap a creature, energy, object or spirit in a bubble outside both time and space, cut off from the world until it ends.
system: A Godlike feat: 20 or more successes, plus 2 per step on the Time-Sphere Timelines chart, and each step adds two layers of Paradox. Fifty years takes at least 24 successes and eight times the normal Paradox.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Sidestep Time
summary: Step sideways out of the timestream so nothing outside can touch you. You can still hit or handle things, but they only feel it once the Effect ends, so a victim gets punched by someone they never saw.
system: Turn by turn only. You cannot cast magick while sidestepped, and anything already inside you (poison, sickness, wounds) keeps working. Bringing someone along costs 2 more successes and 1 more Paradox per person.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity

name: Time Travel
summary: Leave the present and travel forward or back through time, stepping out again in the same place at another time. Long trips can change you so much that you no longer fit into the life you left.
system: Out of combat only. Successes: 2 for each step on the Timelines chart (within a year 1, five years 2, 20 years 3, 50 years 4, 100 years 5, 500 years 6, 1000+ years 10); 50 years back takes 8. Going back adds +3 difficulty, is always vulgar and adds two layers of Paradox per step (50 years back: eight times the usual Paradox). Without an anchor point the trip is one-way. Sending another person a few turns costs 4 successes plus 2 per turn.

source.section: Time Distortion and Travel: Time Immunity
Time Distortion and Travel: Dilating Time
Common Magickal Effects: Time and Distance

name: Read Someone's Emotional State
summary: Get a sense of how another person is feeling right now, either by reading their mind or by sensing their spiritual state.

name: Shift Someone's Mood
summary: Push another character's mood one way or another, by working on their mental currents, on the chemistry of their body, or on both together.
system: Against one target a Mind Effect rolls against their Willpower (at least 4), or Willpower +3 when it makes them do what they do not want. Against mages the difficulty is Willpower +3, against some Night-Folk Willpower +5. Mind influence is normally coincidental.

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Perception and Psychic Powers

name: Read Surface Thoughts
summary: Pick up whatever another character is thinking at the moment, without digging any deeper.
system: Difficulty is the target's Willpower, with 4 as the minimum. A surface read on someone with Willpower 3 is difficulty 4.

name: Read Biological Cues
summary: Read a living creature's body for the chemical and physical signals that betray its fear, arousal, aggression and other reactions.

name: Invade Another's Thoughts and Dreams
summary: Push into someone else's mind: go through their thoughts or step into their dreams while they sleep.

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Perception and Psychic Powers

name: Mass Mind Control
summary: Take hold of a whole crowd's minds at once, or wipe out, completely rebuild or even create a person's consciousness.
system: Large numbers of targets need many successes; see the Magickal Feats chart. Against a group the difficulty follows the normal coincidental or vulgar values rather than one Willpower; a group of mages or Night-Folk is difficulty 8 when you are subtle and 10 when you are blatant.

name: Tweak Body Chemistry
summary: Adjust hormones and pheromones, your own or someone else's, to stir emotions: smell right, dull pain, project raw aggression, or make a person feel uneasy or drawn in. It sways people without controlling their minds.
system: Acts as a coincidental modifier of -1 to -3 on a related mundane roll, and at the Storyteller's call may give automatic success on easy tasks. Needs a paradigm that knows body chemistry; an optional rule asks for Science 3 with a biochemistry specialty.
coincidentalIf: you do not make drastic, obviously magickal changes

name: Puppetry: Take Over a Mind
summary: Override a person's will and run them like a puppet, from a gentle push toward something they half want to a total takeover they will not remember. Rewriting the person from the ground up takes Mind 5.
system: Difficulty is Willpower for a willing subject, Willpower +3 for an unwilling one (mages and Night-Folk +3 or +5, plus another +3 to force Night-Folk). A nudge takes 2-3 successes, forcing an act takes one per point of Willpower, total command 10 (or 2 per Willpower point at Willpower 6+). Prior social feats lower the difficulty.
coincidentalIf: you seduce the subject into your control rather than suddenly jerking the strings

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Perception and Psychic Powers

name: Detect a Lie
summary: Catch a deliberate falsehood, either by noticing the hitch in the liar's thoughts or by reading the tiny tells people give off when they say what they know is untrue. Someone who believes their own words does not read as lying.
system: Simple method: one roll against the target's Willpower. Resisted method: the liar's base difficulty is 4-5 for a plausible lie, 8-10 for an absurd one; the seeker rolls against the liar's Willpower. A liar without fear or conscience may add +3.
coincidentalIf: you are not blatant about it; a long look into the eyes is fine, conjuring a demon of lies is not

name: Lull Someone to Sleep
summary: Coax a person toward sleep with a wave of drowsiness, a firm mental suggestion, or tired body chemistry. They drift off in their own time and can fight it for a while.
system: The target can resist with Willpower rolls, or Stamina to stay awake by sheer toughness. Other people can wake the sleeper. Extra successes or the Magickal Feats chart put several people to sleep.

name: Knock Someone Out Instantly
summary: Drop a target where they stand, either by switching their body over to sleep or with a mental order to sleep at once. They stay out until the Effect ends or you wake them.
system: The target can try to resist as usual. Extra successes or the Magickal Feats chart cover several targets.
coincidentalIf: it comes through something like sleep gas or a knockout blow

name: Plant a Mental Illusion
summary: Plant sights, sounds or other false sensations straight into a target's head. Nobody else perceives them, so the victim may just look crazy.
system: Feats of Illusion: 1 success for one simple sensation, 2 if it moves, 3 for complex and still or two senses, 4 complex and moving, 5 reflexive, 6+ interactive. Lasts a scene; each extra Duration level costs a success. To disbelieve, roll Willpower at 3 (absurd) to 9 (too likely) needing as many successes as the caster.

combos.note: a simple illusion (M20 chart lists Mind 2+)

coincidentalIf: it comes through drugs, hypnosis or some other reason to doubt one's senses, not a stare into the eyes

source.section: Magickal Reference Charts: Feats of Illusion

name: Project a Physical Illusion
summary: Shape light, sound and other forces into an illusion that everyone present can perceive, powered by Prime. A small flicker or noise needs little; a large, elaborate scene needs high ranks.
system: Successes follow the Feats of Illusion chart (1 for one simple sensation up to 6+ for interactive); a fully convincing illusion needs at least 5, a realistic tank 20 or more. Lasts a scene. Close scrutiny (Perception + Alertness) can spot flaws, but disbelief alone does nothing. Cameras see through it unless it is built to fool them.

combos.note: a small trick of light or sound

coincidentalIf: it looks like something that could be real, or onlookers expect special effects from you

source.section: Magickal Reference Charts: Feats of Illusion

name: Nudge Fate and Fortune
summary: Tilt chance in small ways using what is already there: arrive at the perfect moment, decide how dice fall, delay a bus, make a gun run dry. Rank 3 gives finer control. It cannot conjure a taxi from nowhere.
system: Small, likely tweaks are coincidental and need 1-2 successes (an enemy tripping on a crack: difficulty 5). Unlikely results are vulgar and need 5 or more. Coincidentally, the Storyteller decides how the result comes about; picking the exact outcome yourself is vulgar.

name: Scatter or Focus Someone's Thoughts
summary: Work on the odds behind a person's perceptions and nerve reflexes so their thinking falls apart or snaps into sharp focus.

name: Bewitch Someone from a Distance
summary: Work influence magick on a person who is not in front of you. Normally that takes Correspondence alongside the influence Sphere, but a phone, text or email to someone you already have a tie to can replace it, and mass media can reach crowds.
system: Correspondence caps the Effect: Mind 4 at range needs Correspondence 4. Virtual messages reach one person; a mass-media Effect needs at least 10 successes, often 30 or more, works slowly and suits mild ideas better than orders.

combos.note: Correspondence at least equal to the Mind rank used

name: Bind Distant People Together
summary: Tie two or more people in different places to each other: a love spell that links two hearts far apart, or a psychic bond shared by a scattered group.
system: The Data Sphere works the same as Correspondence for this.

name: Bless or Curse a Person or Place
summary: Point the flow of events toward good or bad luck for a person, place or situation. From Entropy 4 you can lay an immediate blessing or curse straight onto a person.
system: Coincidentally you wish for good or ill and the Storyteller decides what happens; naming the exact outcome (ace that interview) is vulgar. A simple blessing needs few successes, a sweeping one more. It lasts the Effect's Duration and touches those near you.

combos.note: nudge events toward good or bad fortune
immediate blessing or curse on a person
M20: luck worked into a living being
M20: a Prime Master's blessing or curse

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Fate and Fortune

name: Lasting Blessing or Curse
summary: Work a blessing or curse into the Pattern of a person, object or place so it follows them after they leave you, like a car that stays unlucky for good.

combos.note: a person, even after they leave
an object such as a car

optional.purpose: set it to go off on a trigger event

name: Binding Oath
summary: Tie a person's luck to a promise they make freely and knowingly, so that breaking it turns their own sense of fate against them. You may talk them into it by any ordinary means, but forced or Mind-planted oaths fail.
system: A vague doom is coincidental and Storyteller-shaped; a specific doom is vulgar but happens. A simple doom takes 1-3 successes, an elaborate one 10 or more. Entropy 1 plus Perception + Awareness spots the oath and any breach. Permanent until broken, released or kept to death.

name: Conceptual Entropy: Plant or Break an Idea
summary: Build up or pick apart an idea in people's heads, through talk and argument backed by Entropy. It works on whole groups if you have their ear; planted ideas spread on their own, broken ones are discredited, and a backlash always follows big pushes.
system: Difficulty Willpower +3 (mages and Night-Folk +5), with social rolls to set up influence. A whim takes 1-2 successes, a simple concept 2-3, a complex idea or deep conviction 4-5, an obsession or philosophy 5 or more.
coincidentalIf: the target reaches their own conclusions rather than having their mind suddenly go haywire

name: Spot Another Mage's Mind Control
summary: Look over someone who is acting strangely and see whether a mage's Mind magick is working on them. Resonance often shows whose signature it is.

source.section: Uncanny Influence: Resistance, Recognition, and Duration

name: Lift Another Mage's Mental Influence
summary: Clear away someone else's mind control or influence from a person, either by unweaving it as countermagick or by removing it outright.
system: Either way you need more successes than the original caster rolled. A target can also shake off an intrusion on their own with Willpower at difficulty 6 by beating the caster's successes.

source.section: Uncanny Influence: Resistance, Recognition, and Duration

name: Trigger-Conditioning
summary: Plant a Mind Effect that lies dormant until a trigger sets it off: a code word, a feeling, an activity or a set time.
system: When the trigger fires, the subject rolls Willpower at difficulty 8; success breaks the conditioning, failure means they carry out the planted command.

combos.note: Mind at the rank of the Effect being planted

source.section: Uncanny Influence: Resistance, Recognition, and Duration

name: Ease Social Rolls with Subtle Mind Magick
summary: Use a quiet, coincidental Mind nudge to make ordinary social actions easier, and alternate it with plain charm and social feats so nobody sees magick at work.
system: Lowers the difficulty of the social roll as per Magick Enhancing Abilities (-1 to -3). Followers from Cult, Retainers or Spies take minor influence at -3 difficulty or without a roll; major influence is at normal difficulty, and traumatic acts on them add +3.

name: Emotional Surge or Sudden Chill
summary: Flood a target with one overwhelming feeling (rage, despair, lust, euphoria) until they lose their judgment, or flip it and drown them in deep calm instead.
system: Each success takes one temporary Willpower; more successes than the target's Willpower rating leaves them in an irrational fit of passion. Difficulty is the target's Willpower, +1 to +3 if the feeling fights their current mood, -1 to -3 if it fits. The Life version uses Stamina +3 as difficulty.

name: Psychic Overload
summary: Swamp a target with sensations and conflicting signals until they are stunned and reeling.
system: Difficulty is the target's Willpower (Stamina +3 for the nerve version). Stuns if successes reach the target's Willpower; each success above it is one turn stunned. A stunned character can still move if attacked but loses one die per success.

combos.note: shut down or overload the nerves and senses

coincidentalIf: it comes through a believable instrument such as loud music or strobe lights

name: Instant Madness or Sanity
summary: Blow apart a victim's grip on reality with hallucinations and wild impulses, or the reverse: snap an insane person back to sanity. Marauders and Malkavians cannot be cured this way.
system: Instant shifts are vulgar; driving someone mad or sane slowly by plausible means can stay coincidental. Derangements are in M20 pp. 649-650.

name: Psychic Blast
summary: Hit a target's mind with a focused bolt of psychic force.
system: A direct attack against the target's Willpower (mages and Night-Folk +3, vampires with Dominate +5), dealing bashing damage per the Base Damage or Duration chart. Vulgar, with the usual Paradox.

source.section: Common Magickal Effects: Perception and Psychic Powers

name: The Psychic Shatter
summary: Rip directly into the Pattern of the target's brain, Scanners style, dealing aggravated damage that armor and tough skin cannot stop.
system: Difficulty is the target's Willpower (+3 or +5 for mages and Night-Folk). Only internal protection like a psychic shield can soak it. A survivor may need a Willpower roll, difficulty equal to health levels lost, to avoid Things Man Was Not Meant to Know. Extremely vulgar.

name: Forge Memories
summary: Make a person forget something, remember what never happened, or recall it differently, by hypnosis, conditioning or a flash from a gadget.
system: Willing or unwitting subjects use Willpower as difficulty, unwilling ones Willpower +3 and may resist. Erasing one small detail takes 1-2 successes; large wipes or overlays take 5 or more and can leave the subject confused and traumatized. At the Storyteller's option Mind 3 can blur a short stretch of time.

name: Awaken the Spirit in an Object
summary: Wake the sleeping spirit inside a thing so it works a little better (a knife that never dulls, a car that starts easily) and exists in the Umbra as well. With Life the same works on microbes; complex creatures are awake already.
system: Needs an animistic paradigm, and the spirit must be won over with offerings, songs or thanks. The edge is minor and story-based; real power needs a Fetish.

name: Invoke Spirit Possession
summary: Put a spirit into an object, a creature or your own body, whether it likes it or not, and use it to influence both the host and the spirit.
system: Sleepers with Willpower 5 or less cannot throw the spirit out. Others get one try a day: an extended resisted roll to 10 successes, each side rolling against the other's Willpower. Optional: -1 difficulty for a deeply compatible spirit and host, +1 for an obviously conflicted pair. Ejecting a spirit you invited yourself is a resisted Willpower roll.

name: Channel a Spirit's Gifts Through Possession
summary: Let an allied spirit into your body and use the bond as the focus for Life magick that matches it: a Wolf spirit giving you fur, quick reflexes or a full wolf shape.

combos.note: small changes such as furry skin
full change into the spirit's animal form

optional.purpose: invite the spirit into yourself without an Allies or Totem bond

name: Exorcise a Possessing Spirit
summary: Drive a possessing spirit out of a person or object and back where it came from, by prayer, ritual or ectoplasm-busting tech. You can also bribe it with your own Quintessence, which is risky.
system: Extended resisted Willpower rolls at difficulty 8, one per hour. The spirit wins at successes equal to your Willpower + Avatar; you need 10 for a minor spirit, 15 for a stronger one, 20+ for a major Umbrood, 30+ for a mighty one. A spirit's botch ejects it; your botch lets it take you over. True Faith acts as Spirit 4 against foes of the faith.

optional.purpose: bribe the spirit: each point of Quintessence given is -1 difficulty (max -3)

name: Spot a Spirit's Mark
summary: Notice the traces a possessing spirit leaves on its host: a limp, a scent, an odd craving, raven-black eyes. A Lore roll may tell you which spirit left it.
system: Without the Sphere a Perception + Awareness roll can still spot it, difficulty set by the spirit's power.

name: Coax a Liar into Giving Herself Away
summary: Trick a liar into revealing the lie, either by working on their mind or by tilting the odds so they are more likely to tell the truth.

combos.note: sway the odds; Entropy 3 sways them harder

name: Compel Someone to Speak the Truth
summary: Make a person tell the truth even though they do not want to.

name: Back a Lie with Magick
summary: Use subtle Mind or Entropy magick to make your own lies go down easier, or to help someone else's lie detection.
system: Lowers the difficulty of the Subterfuge roll as per Magick Enhancing Abilities. The base difficulty of the lie is 4-5 if believable and 8-10 if outrageous, so a small lie gains more than a huge one.

name: Break a Liar's Concentration
summary: Unravel a liar's focus so completely that they can no longer hold the story together and the truth comes out.

name: Tell-Tale Heart Syndrome (The Perry Mason Trick)
summary: Raise a liar's anxiety, squeeze them with circumstance and feed them a growing guilt until they break down and confess, usually in a dramatic outburst. Innocent people sometimes confess too.
system: Uses the normal truth-seeking rolls. Works best with all three Spheres and needs at least two of them. A success ruins the liar's credibility and rattles them emotionally.

name: Hallucinations Through Body Chemistry
summary: Fool any of a person's senses by tampering with the chemistry and nerve signals behind them. You need to know what you are doing for it to produce the hallucination you want.

name: Illusion That Fools Cameras
summary: Build a complex illusion specifically for recording gear so a video camera captures it as real.
system: Also needs a successful roll with several dots in the right Technology Skill. Only very simple, brief illusions fool recordings without this.

name: Immersive Illusion (Holodeck Level)
summary: Create a physical illusion as convincing as reality, one that reacts freely to people, can be touched and creates real sensations. It is still not real.
system: No amount of successes reaches this level with lower ranks. A mental illusion can be immersive without these Spheres.

source.section: Magickal Reference Charts: Feats of Illusion

name: Phantasmal Wounds
summary: Tie a psychic attack to a mental illusion so the victim sees a phantom claw or blade and real injuries appear on their body, however you choose to shape them.
system: Each success above the illusion's base adds two levels of damage.

source.section: Magickal Reference Charts: Feats of Illusion

name: Illusion Backed by Real Force
summary: Put real elemental force behind a physical illusion, so it hits with blasts of wind or steam, or an illusory robot actually picks someone up and flies off with them.
system: Usually bashing damage, lethal or aggravated with things like radiation or steam. Each success above the illusion's base adds two levels of damage. Lifting uses the Forces and Weight chart.

name: Arrange a Dangerous Coincidence
summary: Steer an enemy into a hazard that is already around, like a speeding car or a rotten floorboard. Below rank 4 Entropy does no damage itself, so the hazard does the work; forcing a specific disaster, like collapsing a floor, is vulgar Entropy 4.
system: Coincidentally, the Storyteller decides the hazard and its damage; a likely hazard needs fewer successes than a freak one. Damage per Environmental Hazards in M20.

name: Wave Away an Idea
summary: Make an idea vanish from someone's head with a gesture or a look, skipping the argument.

name: Losing My Religion: Break Someone's Faith
summary: Grind down a single person's faith until it and their will give way. On Night-Folk the result can be devastating, from frenzy and despair to a Harrowing or a flood of Banality.
system: One target only, rolled as vulgar without witnesses. Difficulty is the target's Willpower (mages and Night-Folk +5), +1 per dot of True Faith, which also adds 2 needed successes per dot. Each success removes a temporary Willpower; at 0 the faith breaks until Willpower is fully regained, longer if torture or Mind assaults are added.

name: Shatter a Mage's Paradigm
summary: Turn conceptual entropy on another mage's paradigm until they no longer trust it, so all of their magick counts as vulgar with witnesses: they are their own witness.
system: Needs at least 10 successes against their Willpower +5. Lasts until they regain full Willpower; combined with torture or Mind assaults it can stick until they find their faith again or a new Path.
